destinations.title: Thailand Travel: Destinations, Weather and Entry Requirements
destinations.description: Plan a Thailand vacation with destination ideas, monthly weather, TDAC instructions and entry guidance for U.S. passport holders.
destinations.intro: Picture the vacation you want: unwinding at a good hotel, wandering between temples and cafés, or spending long days by the sea. Think about how you would spend a day in each city or island, then choose the places that appeal to you.
destinations.entryIntro: Traveling to Thailand for a vacation on a U.S. ordinary passport? Start with the passport and visa exemption requirements, then use your flight and hotel reservations to complete your TDAC. If your itinerary requires a visa, find the category that matches your purpose and learn how to apply.
destinations.seasonsIntro: Have a month in mind? Compare the weather for walking around Bangkok’s temples and markets with a beach vacation in Phuket or Koh Samui. Monthly temperatures and rainfall can help you choose a time to travel and decide what to pack.

bangkok.name: Bangkok
bangkok.intro: Spend the day relaxing at a hotel with a pool, then head out for dinner by the river or skyline views from a rooftop. Bangkok suits travelers who want to combine a five-star hotel stay with time exploring the city.

chiang-mai.name: Chiang Mai
chiang-mai.intro: Wander through the Old City’s temple grounds and side streets, stopping at a café that catches your eye. This is a city for taking your time, with a walk and a cup of coffee shaping an easygoing day.

chiang-rai.name: Chiang Rai
chiang-rai.intro: See architecture with striking colors and forms, including the White Temple and Blue Temple. You can experience places you have seen in photographs while exploring northern Thailand’s mountains and temples.

pattaya.name: Pattaya
pattaya.intro: Walk along the beach or relax at your hotel during the day, then sit down to dinner overlooking the sea. Pattaya combines time by the water with the restaurants and sightseeing of a city vacation.

hua-hin.name: Hua Hin
hua-hin.intro: Stay by the sea with your family, take a morning beach walk and browse the markets in the evening. Choose Hua Hin when you would rather leave time for shared meals and rest than fill every hour with sightseeing.

phuket.name: Phuket
phuket.intro: Set aside some days for relaxing at a seaside resort and others for exploring the Old Town. You can enjoy a beach vacation as well as meals and walks along streets lined with colorful buildings.

krabi.name: Krabi
krabi.intro: Walk beside the sea with limestone cliffs rising above the coast. Combine days of beachside rest with boat trips to nearby islands for a vacation that brings you different views of the water.

samui.name: Koh Samui
samui.intro: Have a late breakfast at a seaside resort, stroll along the beach and return to your room for a break. Leave plenty of time for unhurried meals and relaxation with your partner or family.

phi-phi.name: Phi Phi Islands
phi-phi.intro: Discover cliffs rising out of the sea and views opening between the islands. Explore by boat or look out from a viewpoint to experience the Thai island scenery you have seen in photographs.

phangan.name: Koh Phangan
phangan.intro: If you want both a beach break and nights with music, consider Koh Phangan. Choose your beach and travel dates to plan either a lively stay or a quieter vacation.

tao.name: Koh Tao
tao.intro: Curious about the scenery beneath the water as well as along the shore? Try learning to snorkel or dive on Koh Tao, then wind down on the beach in the evening.

lanta.name: Koh Lanta
lanta.intro: Read a book at your seaside accommodation, then walk along the beach as the sun goes down. Koh Lanta suits travelers who want to linger on a favorite stretch of coast rather than seek out a new attraction every day.

samet.name: Koh Samet
samet.intro: Consider Koh Samet if you want to add a short beach break to a Bangkok trip. Walk on white sand and eat by the sea, giving yourself time to relax after exploring the city.

Rainfall drops sharply from November after the wetter months of September and October, and average temperatures in December and January are around 27°C, more comfortable than April’s heat. Average daytime highs still exceed 32°C, so visit temples in the morning, walk by the river near sunset and leave time in between for meals and indoor breaks.

entry.title: Entering Thailand: TDAC and Requirements for U.S. Travelers
entry.description: Prepare for Thailand on a U.S. ordinary passport: visa exemption, TDAC timing, documents and the steps from passport control to the arrivals hall.
entry.intro: Have you chosen your dates for Bangkok or Phuket? If you are vacationing on a U.S. ordinary passport, read the visa exemption conditions first and complete your TDAC for your arrival date. Keep your passport, flights and hotel reservation beside you so you can enter the details accurately. This guide takes you from preflight documents through passport control and baggage claim.

sections.title: Vacationing on a U.S. passport
paragraphs: For tourism on a U.S. ordinary passport, the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington, D.C. states that visa exemption allows **up to 30 days**, effective September 15, 2026. An extension of no more than 30 additional days may be requested, but the immigration officer decides whether to grant it. A companion traveling on another country’s passport must use the rules for that passport.

The maximum period is not a guarantee that every traveler will receive the same permission. After passport control, read the **actual permitted-stay expiration date** recorded in your passport and leave within that period. If you intend to work or study, prepare the visa for that activity instead of relying on tourism entry. Longer stays also need a category suited to your purpose and itinerary.

sections.title: What to have ready before your flight
paragraphs: Keep your passport, flight details and hotel confirmation together. Enter your name on TDAC **exactly as it appears in your passport**, and use the hotel name and English address on your booking. Look at the flight that actually arrives in Thailand: the local arrival date and flight number can differ from the date you leave the United States.

Have your return or onward travel and accommodation details available. If immigration asks where you are staying and when you will leave, explain your actual reservations. You also need to demonstrate adequate travel funds. The embassy’s exemption guidance requires **cash equivalent to 20,000 baht per person or 40,000 baht per family**. This is evidence of travel funds, separate from TDAC, which has no submission fee.

sections.title: Complete TDAC within the three-day arrival window
paragraphs: TDAC is the online arrival card that replaces the paper form. **Non-Thai nationals entering Thailand** by air, land or sea must complete it before immigration. Children and infants need their own records too.

Submit **within the three days before arrival, including the arrival date**. Prepare your passport, flight, Thailand arrival date, accommodation address in English and email address. Download the completed document to your phone so you can open it even if the airport connection is unreliable.
Completing the arrival card does not issue a visa. **TDAC and visa preparation are separate tasks**. If your purpose of travel requires a visa, prepare both the visa and the arrival card.

sections.title: From your aircraft to the arrivals hall
paragraphs: After leaving the aircraft, follow **Immigration / Passport Control** signs. Keep your passport, TDAC confirmation and any required visa easy to reach. Answer questions about your purpose and accommodation using your real travel plans.

Once you clear immigration, read your permitted-stay expiration date. Continue to **Baggage Claim**, collect your bags and pass through customs to the arrivals hall. Follow the declaration procedure if you have goods to declare. Routes differ between Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang and other airports, so also read the guide for your arrival airport.

sections.title: Airside transit and entering Thailand
paragraphs: You do not need TDAC if you **transit without passing through Thai immigration**. If you leave the airport, or pass immigration to collect and recheck baggage, you do need the arrival card.

If you booked separate tickets, ask your airlines before departure whether your bags will be checked through and whether you must pass immigration in Thailand. An itinerary labeled “transit” may still involve entering the country; prepare TDAC whenever that is the actual route.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

faq.q: Do I need both TDAC and a visa?
faq.a: Even when you enter visa-free on a U.S. ordinary passport, you must complete TDAC. TDAC is the arrival declaration; a visa depends on your purpose and eligibility. A qualifying tourism trip can use visa exemption, but a work or study itinerary cannot be prepared using TDAC alone.

faq.q: How long can U.S. citizens stay without a visa?
faq.a: The embassy’s tourism exemption guidance effective September 15, 2026 allows up to 30 days. Check the actual permitted-stay expiration date after immigration. Plan your departure around the permission you receive, rather than treating the maximum as an automatic entitlement.

faq.q: What arrival date goes on TDAC if my flight lands late at night?
faq.a: Use the local Thailand arrival date on your ticket. A long flight from the United States can cross calendar dates, so do not copy your U.S. departure date. Read the arrival date together with the flight number that brings you into Thailand.

entry.title: How to Complete TDAC: Thailand’s Digital Arrival Card
entry.description: Follow the official English mobile TDAC form, from passport and flight fields to accommodation, health declaration, submission, download and corrections.
entry.intro: Completing TDAC on your phone? Put your passport, flight ticket and hotel confirmation beside you, then follow the screens below. Each step explains where names go, which Thailand date to use and how to copy your accommodation address. Once you submit successfully, save the document to your phone so it is easy to show at the airport.

sections.title: Start with the official site and submission window
paragraphs: Check that your address bar reads **tdac.immigration.go.th**. This is the Thai Immigration Bureau’s official website, and **TDAC submission is free**. It is a separate site from Thai e-Visa.

Submit **within the three days before arrival, including the arrival date**. You need a new TDAC every time you enter Thailand; a card from a previous trip cannot be reused. Before starting, have your passport, incoming flight number, local Thailand arrival date, accommodation address in English and email ready.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Read the form in the language you prefer
paragraphs: The site provides language settings, and your phone’s browser may also offer page translation. These controls can appear in different places depending on the phone and browser. English-speaking travelers can use the original English form shown below.

Whichever display language you choose, **enter the details in English**. Copy names and passport numbers from the passport, and use your accommodation’s English booking address. The mobile screenshots below retain the English button and field names so you can find each step.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Choose Arrival Card on the opening screen
paragraphs: For a new submission, select **Arrival Card**. The neighboring **Update Arrival Card** button is for changing a record you have already submitted. Start with Arrival Card when you have not yet submitted this trip.

The opening screen also mentions 90-day reporting and work permits. This does not mean TDAC lasts for 90 days or gives you permission to work. Complete this trip’s arrival declaration through Arrival Card.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Personal Information: use your passport details
paragraphs: Enter your surname under **Family Name** and your given name under **First Name**. If you do not have a middle name in your passport, do not invent one to fill Middle Name. Put each part of the name in its matching field and copy the passport number into Passport No.

Nationality/Citizenship asks for citizenship; Date of Birth, Occupation and Gender ask for your birth date, occupation and gender. Country/Territory of Residence is where you currently live, and City/State of Residence is your city or state. A U.S. citizen living overseas should enter actual citizenship and residence separately.

Visa No. is for a visa already issued to you. **If entering visa-free, do not invent a visa number.** Follow the asterisks to distinguish required fields from optional ones. Phone No. separates the country code from your phone number. Select Continue after completing the page.

In the retained screenshot, Retrieve with Passport is unavailable. If the MRZ-reading feature described in the official guide is not available, enter your details manually. Even when it does read your passport, compare the names and passport number against the document.

sections.title: Arrival Information: enter the flight arriving in Thailand
paragraphs: The trip stage has separate **arrival and departure information for Thailand**. Start with Arrival Information and look at your ticket. Find the local Thailand arrival date and incoming flight number, rather than copying the date you left the United States.

For a vacation arriving on a regular passenger flight, choose **HOLIDAY**, **AIR** and **COMMERCIAL FLIGHT**. These answers describe air travel for a holiday; business, study, land and sea arrivals must reflect their actual circumstances.

Type the English country name or three-letter code, then **select the matching result from the list**. If you boarded the Thailand-bound flight in the United States, search for USA and select USA : THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. Typing a code without choosing its list entry may not set the country.
sections.caption: English mobile Arrival Information screen
fields: Date of Arrival
Enter the local Thailand arrival date from your ticket in YYYY/MM/DD format, or use the calendar. It can differ from your U.S. departure date.
Country/Territory where you Boarded

Select the country where you boarded the flight to Thailand. For a nonstop U.S. departure, choose USA : THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. If you connect abroad, use the country where you board that Thailand-bound flight.
Purpose of Travel
Choose HOLIDAY for a vacation. Use MEETING, BUSINESS or EDUCATION only when they match the trip. OTHERS (PLEASE SPECIFY) requires an explanation in English.
Mode of Travel
Select AIR for a flight, LAND for a land crossing or SEA for a sea arrival. This choice changes the transport options below.
Mode of Transport
Choose COMMERCIAL FLIGHT for a regular passenger flight. PRIVATE/CARGO AIRLINE and OTHERS apply only when they describe your actual transport.
Flight No./Vehicle No.
Copy the airline code and number of the flight arriving in Thailand. This is not a reservation code or seat number. Land and sea travelers enter the relevant transport details.

sections.title: Departure Information: enter your trip out of Thailand
paragraphs: Below the arrival fields is **Departure Information**. Its date and flight number concern **leaving Thailand**, rather than leaving the United States. With a round-trip ticket, copy the local Thailand departure date and flight number of your return flight.

Departure fields have no required asterisk in the retained screen. If you do not yet have a departure plan, do not make up dates or flight numbers. An optional form field does not remove the need to explain your return or onward plans at immigration.
Use **Clear** to remove a departure travel mode chosen by mistake. Read the section headings carefully so you do not confuse the arrival AIR option with departure AIR.
sections.caption: English mobile Departure Information screen
fields: Date of Departure
The local date you leave Thailand, which may differ from the date you arrive back in the United States.
Mode of Travel
Choose AIR, LAND or SEA for the way you leave Thailand. Arrival and departure modes can differ.
Mode of Transport
Choose the actual transport matching your departure mode. A regular return passenger flight is COMMERCIAL FLIGHT.
Flight No./Vehicle No.
Enter the flight or vehicle number leaving Thailand. Compare it with the return ticket rather than copying the arrival flight.
Clear
Resets an incorrectly selected departure travel mode.

sections.title: Accommodation Information: copy your reservation address
paragraphs: Open your hotel reservation and find the **English accommodation address**. This is where you will stay in Thailand, rather than your U.S. home address. Use the booking or hotel’s official address so the place name and administrative areas match.

Required fields may change with accommodation type. In the retained screen, **selecting HOTEL removes the required asterisks from District and Sub-District**. Follow the asterisks on your own form rather than assuming every accommodation type works the same way.

Select Province first, then District, Area, then Sub-District, Sub-Area to make the lower lists available. Choose entries matching the actual hotel address even when names look similar. For accommodation in Bangkok, Province can be BANGKOK.

**I am a transit passenger, I don’t stay in Thailand** concerns transit without a stay. Do not select it simply because you have not booked a hotel. It may be disabled depending on earlier answers. If you are entering Thailand for a stay, provide the actual accommodation details.
sections.caption: English mobile accommodation screen — administrative fields after selecting HOTEL
fields: Type of Accommodation in Thailand
Choose HOTEL, YOUTH HOSTEL, GUEST HOUSE, FRIEND’S HOUSE or APARTMENT to match your stay. Give the requested explanation when choosing OTHERS.
Province
Select the province or Bangkok area containing your accommodation, rather than the location of the airport.
District, Area
Choose the district in the hotel’s address after selecting Province. Whether it is mandatory depends on the accommodation type.
Sub-District, Sub-Area
Choose the smaller administrative area shown in the address. Select the parent district before using this list.
Post Code
Use the accommodation’s Thai postal code. Compare any automatically filled code with the booking. This field has no required asterisk in the retained screen.
Address

Enter the property name and actual building number, street and English address. Choosing administrative areas does not complete the street address. The retained field shows a 215-character limit, so keep the property name and real location information when arranging a long address.

sections.title: Health Declaration: countries visited in the past two weeks
paragraphs: The health declaration asks for **countries or territories where you stayed during the two weeks before arrival**. If you have been living in the United States and leave directly, select the United States. Include any other countries where you actually stayed during that period. This field is not for Thai cities you plan to visit.

Type an English country name or code and choose the matching result. Citizenship, residence, the country of boarding and recent stays are different questions. If you are traveling between countries, do not automatically copy the same country into every field.

A vaccination notice refers to Thai Ministry of Public Health requirements. The official guide explains that **additional health information may be requested** depending on recent countries, boarding country, nationality or flight. Read and answer the questions shown for your own journey. The retained screenshot illustrates a route using Korea and does not establish that every traveler sees identical extra fields.

Select **Preview** when you finish. Previous returns to the preceding step, while Add Other Travelers adds another traveler’s record. Use each person’s actual travel history rather than copying one traveler’s countries to everyone.
sections.caption: English mobile health declaration — countries stayed in during the preceding two weeks
fields: Countries/territories where you stayed within two weeks before arrival
Select the countries and territories where you actually stayed during the two weeks before entering Thailand, not future Thai destinations or the authority issuing your passport.
If additional health questions or evidence are requested
Read the displayed requirements and provide your own actual health and travel details. Do not copy answers from an example with different eligibility.
Preview / Previous / Add Other Travelers
Preview reviews entries, Previous returns to the prior step and Add Other Travelers adds another person. Use each traveler’s passport and actual trip details.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Preview: review your details and enter your email
paragraphs: Review your name, passport number, nationality and birth date, plus **arrival date, boarding country, arrival flight and accommodation address**. Use **Edit** to correct anything wrong. EXAMPLE in the screenshot is demonstration data; no actual declaration was submitted.

Enter an email address you can receive mail at in the **email field** near the bottom. It is not a name field: read the spelling and both sides of the @ sign. Being able to open that inbox on your phone makes it easier to find the completed document.
Read **Terms and conditions**, check the box if you agree and choose **Submit**. The submission button is disabled without the required agreement. Reaching Preview does not complete submission.
If an error appears or the completed document does not show, do not treat the declaration as successfully submitted. Look for the actual success notice and TDAC document before saving them.

Please specify an email to send Thailand Digital Arrival Card

I have read and accepted the Terms and conditions
Read the linked terms and check the box yourself only if you agree.
Submit
Submit after review, email entry and the required agreement. Then look for confirmation and the actual document.

sections.title: After submission: save the TDAC document to your phone
paragraphs: After successful submission, look for the **success notice and TDAC download**. The official video shows both. The retained image is a **completion example from that official video**, captured in a mobile browser. The video itself uses an older desktop screen, so its layout can differ from the current mobile form.

Download your document and compare the name, passport information and arrival date with your trip. Keep the declaration number, QR code and other confirmation details, and find the emailed copy too. Never use the sample number or QR code in the video as your own arrival document.

Save the file on your phone so it **opens without internet access**. Keeping the actual file, rather than just an email link, helps when the arrival airport connection is unreliable. You can also bring a printed copy if useful.

Have the confirmation available at entry and keep it during your stay. **TDAC confirmation is not a visa or permission to enter.** You still need to satisfy your visa or exemption conditions and pass immigration.

sections.title: Updating a TDAC you already submitted
paragraphs: Choose **Update Arrival Card** from the opening screen. The retained search screen asks for the TDAC number, birth date, arrival date and nationality. Fill them in using your confirmation and passport, then select **Search**.

The official FAQ says **passport name, passport number, nationality and birth date cannot be changed** and advises a new form with correct details for those errors. Its release history separately states that passport-number editing was enabled; these statements conflict. For an incorrect passport number, seek clarification from Immigration rather than relying on an assumed editing rule. Correct other editable information, such as accommodation, before entry, resubmit and save the resulting document.
This screen searches for a declaration already submitted. If you have not submitted one yet, return to Arrival Card and start a new declaration instead of looking for a TDAC number.

faq.q: Is TDAC free?
faq.a: Yes. There is no fee to submit TDAC on the Thai Immigration Bureau’s official site. Check that the address reads tdac.immigration.go.th before starting.

faq.q: Can I use the English form?
faq.a: Yes. The screenshots here show the English mobile form. Regardless of your chosen display language, enter details in English using the passport and your accommodation’s English booking address.

faq.q: Do children and visa-exempt travelers need TDAC?
faq.a: Yes. U.S. travelers using visa exemption, children and infants each need a TDAC record. The requirement applies to non-Thai entrants. Transit without passing through Thai immigration does not require TDAC.

faq.q: Does completing TDAC issue a Thai visa?
faq.a: No. The arrival card and a visa are separate preparations. For visa-free tourism on a U.S. ordinary passport, satisfy the exemption conditions. For a purpose requiring a visa, obtain the appropriate visa as well.

faq.q: Can I correct a misspelled name?
faq.a: Submit a new declaration with the correct name. The FAQ excludes passport name, passport number, nationality and birth date from editing, although its passport-number release note conflicts with that list. Ask Immigration about a passport-number error; use Update Arrival Card for other editable details before entry, then resubmit and save the result.

faq.q: Does the flight field mean my reservation code?
faq.a: No. Flight No./Vehicle No. needs the airline code and number of the flight arriving in Thailand. It is not the booking reference or seat number.

faq.q: Is the departure date the day I arrive home?
faq.a: No. Date of Departure under Departure Information is the local date your flight leaves Thailand. It may differ from the date you arrive in the United States; read the Thailand departure part of your ticket.

faq.q: Are District and Sub-District required after choosing HOTEL?
faq.a: The retained screen removes their required asterisks after HOTEL is selected. Requirements can vary with accommodation type, so follow the asterisks on your actual form.

faq.q: Does the two-week health question mean Thai cities I will visit?
faq.a: No. Choose countries and territories where you actually stayed during the two weeks before entering Thailand. It is not a list of future destinations.

faq.q: Am I finished when Preview opens?
faq.a: No. Preview lets you review the form before submission. Enter your email, read the terms, submit after agreeing and look for the success notice and actual TDAC document.

entry.title: Thailand Visa Types: Tourism, Work, Study and Longer Stays
entry.description: Compare visa exemption with tourist visas, DTV, work, study and retirement categories, and learn the Thai e-Visa application process for U.S. travelers.
entry.intro: A vacation, a job and a course of study call for different entry preparations. On a U.S. ordinary passport, start by seeing whether your vacation qualifies for visa exemption. Tourism entry cannot replace the permission needed for work or study. Decide what you will do and how long you will stay, then prepare the category that fits.

sections.title: Visa exemption, TDAC and a visa have different roles
paragraphs: **Visa exemption** lets eligible travelers enter without obtaining a visa in advance. **TDAC** is the online arrival declaration. A **visa** is issued for a purpose such as tourism, work or study. Submitting TDAC does not mean you have received a visa.

For U.S. ordinary passport tourism, the embassy states a maximum visa-exempt stay of 30 days under the scheme effective September 15, 2026. Companions with other passports need their own nationality’s conditions. Reading an American English guide does not make U.S. passport eligibility apply to another nationality.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Choose the category for your actual purpose
paragraphs: First decide what you will do in Thailand, then find the matching category below. Thai e-Visa separates tourism, work, study and other purposes. Each category has its own eligibility and documents; similar names do not make their conditions interchangeable. Read the detailed requirements for your intended activity.
fields: Tourist Visa
For tourism and vacations; distinguish single-entry and multiple-entry conditions.
Work & Business
For the relevant employment or business purpose. Tourism exemption and TDAC do not give permission to work.
Studying / Non-Immigrant ED
For study at an educational institution and the applicable education or training purpose.
Retirement / Non-Immigrant O or O-A
For eligible retirees meeting the relevant age and financial requirements. Conditions differ by category.
DTV / Destination Thailand Visa
For qualifying workcation and Thai soft-power activities, among the applicable purposes. It is a different category from a tourist visa.
Transit Visa
For qualifying transit, sports or crew purposes and the relevant eligibility.
LTR / Long-Term Resident
A long-term residence category for applicants who meet its eligibility requirements.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Apply online through Thai e-Visa
paragraphs: Create an account at **thaievisa.go.th**, complete the application, upload the required documents, finish payment and submit. Monitor the dashboard and your email for requests for more documents. Once approved, save the confirmation sent by email.

Use the Thai embassy or consulate responsible for where you actually reside and apply. The United States has separate Washington, D.C., Los Angeles, New York and Chicago jurisdictions. U.S. citizenship alone does not make every mission available from anywhere, and the Washington embassy cannot issue a visa to someone already in Thailand. The Los Angeles document examples in this guide apply only to applicants within that consulate’s jurisdiction.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Visa validity and permitted stay are different
paragraphs: Visa validity is the period in which you can use the visa to enter Thailand. Permitted stay is the time immigration allows you to remain after entry. Even a single-entry tourist visa has a validity period separate from its stay allowance.

A visa does not automatically let you remain until its own final validity date. After immigration, read the **actual permitted-stay expiration date** in your passport and plan departure accordingly. If you need an extension, apply separately before the permission expires and undergo the required assessment. Applying alone does not extend your stay.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

faq.q: Do U.S. citizens always need a tourist visa?
faq.a: No. A U.S. ordinary passport holder who meets the tourism exemption conditions can travel without a tourist visa. Work, study and a longer itinerary may need a different category and preparation. Companions holding other passports cannot automatically use U.S. eligibility.

faq.q: Is DTV the same as a tourist visa?
faq.a: No. DTV and tourist visas are separate categories. DTV includes qualifying workcation and Thai soft-power purposes, while a tourist visa is for tourism. Read the eligibility and documents for the activity you actually intend.

faq.q: Do I submit my passport at the embassy?
faq.a: The U.S. Thai missions use Thai e-Visa for online applications and delivery. The Washington embassy says no passport or original supporting documents need to be mailed or submitted in person. First confirm the mission responsible for your residence, then follow its current instructions.

entry.title: Thailand Tourist Visa: Single Entry, Multiple Entry and e-Visa
entry.description: Compare tourist visa validity and permitted stay, then prepare the passport, reservations, U.S. mission documents, fees and Thai e-Visa application.
entry.intro: You do not need to start by applying for a tourist visa if your vacation on a U.S. ordinary passport qualifies for visa exemption. Compare your trip length with the exemption first. If you need a tourist visa, consider how many times you plan to enter. The document and fee examples below are specifically from the Royal Thai Consulate-General in Los Angeles; travelers in other jurisdictions must follow their own Thai mission.

sections.title: Single entry and multiple entry
paragraphs: Single and multiple entry differ in the number of visits and the period in which the visa can be used. The Los Angeles tourism and leisure guidance states **single entry: three months of visa validity; multiple entry: six months**, with **up to 60 days per entry**. Six-month validity does not mean you can stay six uninterrupted months.

Los Angeles also describes the possibility of an **additional 30-day extension**, bringing a stay to no more than 90 days from entry. Contact Thai Immigration to apply: an extension requires approval and is not granted merely because you submit a request. Read the actual permission recorded in your passport and arrange any necessary extension before it expires.
fields: Single-entry tourist visa
Three months of validity; up to 60 days of stay on entry.
Multiple-entry tourist visa
Los Angeles guidance: six months of validity; no more than 60 days per stay.
Extension
An additional 30 days may be requested from Thai Immigration; approval is required.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: Applicants and supporting documents
paragraphs: For the **Los Angeles consular jurisdiction**, upload a clear passport biodata page, a photograph taken within six months, current-location evidence such as a driver’s license, bank statement or proof of stay, a named flight itinerary into and out of Thailand and accommodation evidence. The passport must be valid for at least six months from travel. Upload large, clear JPEG or PDF files no bigger than 3 MB.

The Los Angeles tourism and leisure page asks for **the last three months of savings or checking statements, with an ending balance of at least $700 per person or $2,000 per family**, showing the applicant’s name and date. A family or joint statement also needs proof of relationship, such as a birth or marriage certificate. These are visa-application bank documents, separate from cash evidence at entry. Older Los Angeles tourist and METV pages display different financial lists; use the current category and the documents requested for your application, and ask the consulate if those differ.

Additional documents apply to **non-U.S. citizens and minors under 20**. Non-U.S. citizens provide the permanent resident card or valid U.S. visa and applicable employment or student evidence; an employment letter must be hand-signed by HR or a manager, rather than a pay stub, job offer or acceptance letter. Self-employed applicants provide business registration, license or personal/business tax returns showing income; students provide full-time status evidence (I-20). For minors, the page lists a birth certificate, parents’ marriage certificate or notarized sole-custody order, and both parents’ or guardians’ passports or ID. A minor traveling alone needs notarized consent from both parents or guardians; when traveling with one parent, the other parent must provide consent.

The flight itinerary must show the applicant’s name, dates, airports and flight number. Accommodation evidence can include bookings or an invitation from family or friends in Thailand. Supporting materials issued outside Thailand and the United States need certified English translations with the consular or Ministry of Foreign Affairs notarization specified by Los Angeles. Read the actual form’s requests instead of replacing them with another country’s document list.

Consular officers may ask for more documents or reject an application. Uploading documents is not approval, and applying outside the consulate’s jurisdiction is listed as a reason for refusal. Use the mission responsible for your residence; this Los Angeles example does not establish one document list for all four U.S. missions.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: From the online application to your approval document
paragraphs: Create your account at **thaievisa.go.th** and choose the actual nationality, location, passport type and tourism purpose. If passport reading fills the form automatically, compare first, middle and last names and the passport details against your document.

Upload the required documents, complete the fee procedure and **submit the application**. Los Angeles lists **$40 for single entry and $200 for multiple entry**; these fees apply to Los Angeles applications; follow the fee displayed by your responsible mission. Visa fees are nonrefundable, so check the passport type and all entries before payment and submission.

After submission, monitor the dashboard and email and respond to requests for additional documents. Save the approved e-Visa confirmation and prepare a printed copy for airline and immigration checks. The Los Angeles tourism and leisure page says processing typically takes **about 15 business days**; its older pages describe a minimum of 15 business days. The current page recommends applying at least 30 days before departure, generally no more than 90 days ahead because many visas run from issue. A status update after additional documents may take 3–5 business days. These are planning instructions, **not a promised issue date**.

verificationEvidence.review: U.S. ordinary passport scope; U.S. mission application conditions identified separately. TDAC original screenshot observations retained.

sections.title: You still need TDAC with a tourist visa
paragraphs: Even after your tourist visa is approved, **complete TDAC separately**. Submit it on the official site within the three days before arrival, including the arrival date, and save the completed document to your phone.

At the airport, keep your passport and visa confirmation ready. After passport control, read the actual permitted-stay expiration date. Your departure must fit the stay granted at entry, rather than simply the date the visa itself stops being valid.

faq.q: Do U.S. citizens need a Thai tourist visa?
faq.a: If your U.S. ordinary passport vacation meets the visa exemption conditions, a separate tourist visa is unnecessary. For an itinerary needing a visa, choose the category that matches your passport, purpose and stay conditions.

faq.q: Does a multiple-entry visa let me stay six months at once?
faq.a: No. The six months in Los Angeles METV guidance is the period in which the visa can be used. Its stated stay is no more than 60 days per entry, rather than six uninterrupted months. Plan departure using the permission recorded after immigration.

faq.q: What are the tourist visa fees for U.S. applicants?
faq.a: The Los Angeles tourist visa page lists $40 for single entry and $200 for multiple entry. The fees are nonrefundable; confirm the fee shown by your responsible mission and the actual e-Visa application before paying. Follow the fee displayed for your actual application and responsible mission.

faq.q: Can I travel as soon as I submit the application?
faq.a: Submission is not visa approval. Read your dashboard and email and wait for the approval document if your trip needs a visa. Additional-document requests can extend the process, and a published processing period does not guarantee a particular issue date.
